title: Reducing pieces in Laczkovich circle-squaring decomposition

problemStatement.formal: TranslationEquidecomposableN(A,B,n) asks for n translation-congruent pieces from A to B; for equal-area disk and square, the file proves no 0-piece or 1-piece decomposition and records 3 \le minPieceCount \le 10^50 from external bounds.
problemStatement.plain: Laczkovich proved that a circle and square of equal area can be decomposed into ~10^50 translation-congruent pieces. But how few pieces actually suffice? This file formalizes the minimum piece count problem, proves 0-piece and 1-piece impossibility (the latter via a diagonal argument and π > 3), proves transitivity of translation congruence, and states the known bounds: at least 3 (topological obstruction) and at most 10^50 (Laczkovich) or 10^5 (Marks-Unger, with Borel pieces).
whyMatters: Circle squaring turns geometric area equality into a precise finite equidecomposition question.
The Lean development proves the small-piece impossibilities while treating the deep Laczkovich and topological bounds as axioms.
The metadata should separate the verified one-piece obstruction from the external high-complexity decomposition theorems.

proven: `iUnion_fin_one_eq`, `mem_translateBy_iff`, `not_one_equidecomposable`, `translation_congruent_trans`, `piece_count_lower_bound`, and `piece_count_in_range` package the small-piece and range facts.
open: `minPieceCount`, `minPieceCount_achieves`, `minPieceCount_is_min`, `laczkovich_upper_bound`, and `lower_bound_three` are axioms in `Erdos1124OQ01.lean`; the file has zero sorries.
knownResults.goal: Expose the formal equidecomposition vocabulary and small lower-bound proofs while keeping the deep circle-squaring bounds axiom-backed.
